description: The .NET runtime, the process, HTTP in and out, the Npgsql client and Hangfire of the WojtusDiscord bot. Job wojtusdiscord; container memory from the host.
title: WojtusDiscord / Runtime & HTTP

options.content: **Is the process healthy and is HTTP fast?** .NET runtime, HTTP in and out, the public URL probe, the Npgsql pool, Hangfire, traces.

panels.title: Uptime, 7 d

targets.expr: 1 - (1 - avg_over_time((min(wojtus_gateway_connected{job="wojtusdiscord"}) or on () (0 * max(up{job="wojtusdiscord"})))[7d:1m])) * count_over_time((min(wojtus_gateway_connected{job="wojtusdiscord"}) or on () (0 * max(up{job="wojtusdiscord"})))[7d:1m]) / 10080

panels.description: 1 minus the time each part was seen down, as a share of the full 7 days: bot process, Discord gateway, public URL, Postgres. Green from 99.9% (10 minutes down in a week), yellow from 99%. A deploy restart counts as down time: about 15 s, 0.0025% of a week, so a few deploys a day stay green and a crash loop does not. Time before a series existed counts as up.

panels.title: Uptime, 30 d

targets.expr: sum by (server_address, http_response_status_code, error_type)(sum_over_time(((http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{job="wojtusdiscord",error_type!=""} - (((last_over_time(http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{job="wojtusdiscord",error_type!=""}[10m] offset 1m) and on (job, instance) (wojtus_process_uptime_seconds{job="wojtusdiscord"} > 660)) or (http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{job="wojtusdiscord",error_type!=""} offset 1m and on (job, instance) (wojtus_process_uptime_seconds{job="wojtusdiscord"} <= 660))) and on (job, instance) (wojtus_process_start_time_seconds{job="wojtusdiscord"} == last_over_time(wojtus_process_start_time_seconds{job="wojtusdiscord"}[10m] offset 1m))) >= 0) or (http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{job="wojtusdiscord",error_type!=""} + 0))[$__interval:1m]))

defaults.noValue: No outbound request failed

panels.description: Outbound requests that failed, per interval: a 4xx or 5xx status, a timeout or a connection error.

panels.title: Pool connections by state

defaults.noValue: No samples in this time range

panels.description: Connections of the Npgsql pool, idle and in use, stacked. The pool maximum is 100. 'used' near the maximum means a connection leak or a stuck job.

panels.title: Commands executing

defaults.noValue: No slash command yet

panels.description: Database commands in flight at the scrape instant. Npgsql exports no count of requests that wait for a connection.

panels.title: Command duration

defaults.noValue: No slash command yet

panels.description: Duration of database commands as the driver measures it, network time included. A dot is one request with a trace (an exemplar): click it to open the trace in Tempo. Only a request inside a kept trace has one.

panels.title: Bytes read and written

defaults.noValue: No samples in this time range

panels.description: Bytes the driver read from and wrote to Postgres per second.

panels.title: Commands per second

defaults.noValue: No slash command yet

panels.description: Database commands the bot completed per second.

panels.title: Connection open time

defaults.noValue: No new connection opened

panels.description: Mean time to open a new physical connection. No point when the pool opens none.

panels.title: Hangfire jobs by state

defaults.noValue: No samples in this time range

panels.description: Jobs in each Hangfire state, read from the database at most every 30 s. 'succeeded' is left out: it is a lifetime total and hides the other states.

panels.title: Succeeded jobs per hour

defaults.noValue: No samples in this time range

panels.description: Jobs that succeeded in the last hour. The succeeded state is a lifetime total in the Hangfire tables, so a bot restart does not reset it.

panels.title: Hangfire servers
panels.description: Hangfire servers alive, the highest value of the last 2 minutes: the first read after a bot start is 0. The bot runs one.

panels.title: Recurring jobs
panels.description: Hangfire recurring jobs registered.

panels.title: Spans by name

defaults.noValue: No spans in this time range

panels.description: Spans per interval by span name: inbound requests, database commands and outbound calls inside a kept trace. From Tempo's metrics generator (source=tempo). Tempo holds only traces with a request or a conversation turn as root.

panels.title: Span duration p95 by name

defaults.noValue: No spans in this time range

panels.description: 95th percentile span duration by span name. From Tempo's metrics generator (source=tempo). Tempo holds only traces with a request or a conversation turn as root.

panels.title: Spans with an error status

defaults.noValue: No span with an error status

panels.description: Spans per interval that ended with an error status. Empty means no span failed. From Tempo's metrics generator (source=tempo). Tempo holds only traces with a request or a conversation turn as root.

panels.title: Service graph requests

defaults.noValue: No spans in this time range

panels.description: Calls between services that Tempo derives from the spans: user to bot, bot to Postgres.

panels.title: Trace export failures
